'''Richard M. Weiner''' (6 February 1930 – 13 August 2020<ref>Nachricht in der [https://www.op-marburg.de/Marburg/Der-Marburger-Physiker-Richard-M.-Weiner-ist-im-Alter-von-90-Jahren-gestorben ''Oberhessischen Presse'' Marburg] vom 30. August 2020; Seite seines [https://literaturwissenschaft.de/buch/tagebuch-eines-denkcomputers.html Verlags]</ref>) was a professor of [[theoretical physics]] at the [[University of Marburg]] in [[Marburg]], Germany and an associate of the Laboratoire de Physique Théorique at [[Paris-Sud University]] in [[Orsay]], France.

==Biography==
Weiner was born 1930 in [[Chernivtsi|Cernăuți]], [[Kingdom of Romania]] (presently [[Chernivtsi]], Ukraine). He was a survivor of the Chernivtsi ghetto during World War II. He then moved to [[Bucharest]], where he studied physics at the [[University of Bucharest]]. In a paper from 1956, he predicted the phenomenon of [[isomeric shift]], his calculations showing that it should be measurable by [[atomic spectroscopy]].<ref name="isomeric"/> Weiner got his PhD in Physics at the University of Bucharest in 1958, and from 1951 to 1968 he worked as a research scientist at the Physics Institute of the [[Romanian Academy of Sciences]]. Because of his intention to leave the [[Communist Romania|Romanian communist regime]], he was retrograded and denied an exit [[visa (document)|visa]], being one of the first [[refusenik]]s of [[Central Europe|Central]] and [[Eastern Europe]]. His 1969 flight from communist Romania and joining [[CERN]] in [[Geneva]] made headlines in the media.<ref name="Analogies">
{{cite book
 |author=Richard M. Weiner
 |year=2008
 |title=Analogies in Physics and Life, A Scientific Autobiography
 |publisher=[[World Scientific]]
 |doi=10.1142/6350
 |isbn=978-981-270-470-2
 |url=https://doi.org/10.1142/6350 
}}</ref>

==Work==
Richard Weiner predicted the [[isomeric shift]]<ref name="isomeric">
{{cite journal
 |author=R. M. Weiner
 |year=1956
 |title=Nuclear isomeric shift on spectral lines
 |journal=[[Nuovo Cimento]]
 |volume=4 |issue=6
 |page=1587
 |doi=10.1007/bf02746390
|bibcode=1956NCim....4.1587W|s2cid=122616293
 }}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=R. M. Weiner
 |year=1959
 |title=Charge Distribution of Excited Isomeric Nuclei and Atomic Spectra (The Nuclear Isomeric Shift)
 |journal=[[Physical Review]]
 |volume=114 |issue=1
 |page=256
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.114.256
|bibcode = 1959PhRv..114..256W |osti=4297429
 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 |author=R. M. Weiner
 |year=1958
 |title=Ядерная изомерия и атомные спектры
 |journal=[[Zhurnal Eksperimental'noi i Teoreticheskoi Fiziki]]
 |volume=35 |issue=1 |pages=284–286
}} translated in {{cite journal
 |author=R. M. Weiner
 |year=1959
 |title=Nuclear Isomerism and Atomic Spectra
 |journal=[[Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Physics]]
 |volume=8
 |issue=1
 |pages=196–197
 |url=http://www.jetp.ac.ru/cgi-bin/dn/e_008_01_0196.pdf
 |access-date=2018-07-17
 |archive-date=2018-07-18
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180718001329/http://www.jetp.ac.ru/cgi-bin/dn/e_008_01_0196.pdf
 |url-status=dead
 }}</ref> which has found wide applications in many fields of physics.<ref>
{{cite conference
 |author=D. A. Shirley
 |year=1961
 |title=Nuclear Applications of Isomeric Shifts
 |editor1=D. H. Compton  |editor2=A. H. Schoen
 |book-title=Proceedings of the International Conference on the Mössbauer Effect
 |page=258
 |publisher=[[John Wiley & Sons]]
 |location=Saclay
}}</ref><ref>
{{cite book
 |author=S. L. Ruby
 |year=1978
 |editor1=G. K. Shenoy |editor2=F. E. Wagner
 |title=Mössbauer Isomer Shifts
 |page=1
 |publisher=[[Elsevier|North Holland]]
}}</ref> He also predicted the [[hot spot effect in subatomic physics]]<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=R. M. Weiner
 |year=1974
 |title=Asymmetry in Peripheral Production Processes
 |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]]
 |volume=32 |page=630
 |doi= 10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.630
|bibcode = 1974PhRvL..32..630W
 |issue=11 }}</ref> and has made contributions to the theory of [[Bose–Einstein correlations]] being also the author of the only textbook on Bose–Einstein correlations.<ref>
{{cite book
 |author=R. M. Weiner
 |year=2000
 |title=Introduction to Bose–Einstein Correlations and Subatomic Interferometry
 |publisher=[[John Wiley & Sons]]
|bibcode=2000ibcs.book.....W
 }}</ref> He was the initiator and co-organizer of the series of meetings [[LESIP]].<ref>
{{cite book
 |author=D. Scott |author2=R. M. Weiner
 |year=1985
 |title=Local Equilibrium in Strong Interaction Physics (LESIP I)
 |publisher=[[World Scientific]]
 |isbn=9971-978-06-7
}}</ref><ref>
{{cite book
 |author=M. Plümer |author2=S. Raha |author3=R. M. Weiner
 |year=1990
 |title=Correlations and Multiparticle Production-CAMP, (LESIP IV)
 |publisher=[[World Scientific]]
 |isbn=981-02-0331-4
}}</ref> He also published a book titled ''Analogies in Physics and Life, A scientific Autobiography''.<ref name="Analogies"/>

He supervised Ph.D. theses by Norbert Stelte, Michael Plümer, Udo Ornik, Fernando Navara, Bernhard Schlei, and Nelly Arbex, and had as postdoctoral collaborators among others Sibaji Raha, Apostolos Vourdas, Fred Pottag, and Leonid Razumov.

Weiner had over 180 publications in scientific journals and books. He also published a science-fiction novel in German, ''Das Miniatom-Projekt''.<ref>
{{cite book
 |author=Richard M. Weiner
 |year=2007
 |title=Das Miniatom-Projekt
|language=de}}</ref><ref name="Frankfurter">Frankfurter Rundschau, February 14, 2007.</ref><ref>Neue Zürcher Zeitung, October 31, 2007.</ref> He was asked for interviews, among others by the [[Frankfurter Rundschau]]<ref name="Frankfurter"/> and was invited by [[Hessischer Rundfunk]] within the series ''[[Doppelkopf]]'' dedicated to renowned personalities.{{cn|date=September 2024}}
